findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "paper_results" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: sota_papers, conference_papers, api_get_llm · Private data: benchmark_timeline, sota_changelog, sota_alarm, list_views, fetch · Public sink: compare_on_benchmark, citation_walk, author, author_papers, coauthor_network · Destructive: sota_with_code.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: sota_papers, conference_papers, api_get_llm · Private data: benchmark_timeline, sota_changelog, sota_alarm, list_views, fetch · Public sink: compare_on_benchmark, citation_walk, author, author_papers, coauthor_network · Destructive: sota_with_code

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
